newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary NYBB keeps 'long-term buy' on OTP.
newsitem.headline: Hungary NYBB keeps 'long-term buy' on OTP.

text.p: Hungarian securities house New York Broker Budapest said on Wednesday it maintained a "long-term buy" recommendation on shares in OTP Bank and added a "short-term speculative buy" rating.
"Our current short-term buy recommendation is based on technical grounds only, therefore it is speculative," said analyst Gabriella Bor in a company update, dated July 1.
"In the long-term, however, the buy is underscored by both (fundamental and technical) sides," she added.
On Wednesday shares in OTP, Hungary's largest commercial bank, jumped to a new record high of 5,220 forints, before they retreated to close at 5,150 forints, up 200.
On the fundamental side, Bor said the bank's registered capital guaranteed that OTP should not have to tap international markets for loans in the coming years, and has reduced its bad debts.

She said that on Hungary's growing retail market banks handle two million accounts of the country's total population of ten million. "This number (two million) might reach five to eight million in the coming years," Bor added.
OTP's market share in retail banking was 57 percent at the end of 1996.
She said that on technical grounds, OTP's current price rally might go as far as 5,500 to 5,700 forints.
"In the short term this is a 10 to 13 percent price gain, but it is speculative," she said, adding she expected a year-end price level of 5,800 to 6,000 forints.
